title: Champions League players to wear new ‘debut patches’ in 2026-27 season
content:
‘Debut patches’ will be appearing for the first time in the 2026-27 men’s Champions League campaign as part of an agreement between Fanatics and UEFA, European soccer’s governing body.

Players appearing for the first time in the competition will have a small patch displayed on the sleeve of their jersey, with the word ‘debut’ being incorporated into the Champions League’s ‘starball’ logo.

After the match, the patch will be retrieved and transferred to Topps — the trading card company owned by Fanatics — and integrated into a unique trading card that is also signed by the player. The patches will be authenticated before entering packs.

The Champions League is the highest level of international club competition in Europe and features 36 teams from across the continent that qualify through their domestic league season (or by winning the Europa League, UEFA’s secondary competition). This season’s competition gets underway on Sept. 8.

Players that come off the bench during games to make their debut will be eligible to receive the patches but those who are unused substitutes after being named in the squad for the first time will have to wait for their actual first appearance.

It is expected that the program will be rolled out in the Women’s Champions League from the 2027-28 season.

The campaign is another foray into soccer for Fanatics, with the Debut patch campaign appearing at this summer’s World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico. The program originated in Major League Baseball and has since expanded to include the NFL, NBA, Bundesliga (German soccer’s top division), Formula 1, MLS, UFC and WWE.

UEFA and Fanatics are also set to announce a six-year extension to their current partnership until 2033, a deal facilitated by Relevent Football Partners, UC3’s exclusive global sales and marketing agency.

“Renewing our partnership with Fanatics for UEFA club competitions reflects the strength of our collaboration and our shared commitment to delivering best-in-class products for fans and collectors globally,” said UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin. “Fanatics know how to make big moments feel special. We are excited for what’s next.”

The trading cards are one-of-one and therefore highly coveted, with Pittsburgh Pirates pitcher Paul Skenes’ debut card setting the record for the highest public sale in March 2025, when Dick’s Sporting Goods paid $1.1 million for the item.

The Athletic reported on Friday that reigning NBA Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg’s debut patch card will go to auction through Fanatics Collect, after the owner rejected multiple offers from Flagg’s team, the Dallas Mavericks, and multi-million-dollar cash offers from individual collectors.

Along with the debut cards of the Charlotte Hornets’ Kon Kneuppel and San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper, the sale of Flagg’s card is expected to comfortably clear the benchmark set by Skenes’ card, and it could also challenge the highest known sale for an ultra-modern (2017-present) basketball card — the $5.1 million sale of the unique 2023-24 Prizm Black parallel Victor Wembanyama rookie card in May.

While the World Cup debut patches will not be obtainable until at least 2031 (when global soccer’s governing body FIFA’s deal with Panini expires and their agreement with Fanatics starts), the Champions League patches are expected to be available this season, due to UEFA’s ongoing deal with Fanatics and extension.

For example, Flagg made his NBA debut on Oct. 10, 2025 and the card was pulled on Aug. 10 this year.

With the Champions League regarded as Europe’s most prestigious club competition, many of the continent’s top players have already appeared in the tournament. However, there are some players that have changed clubs in the transfer window and are in line to make their Champions League debut, such as new Real Madrid arrival Yan Diomande, who joined the club from German club RB Leipzig in a €140 million deal. Manchester United’s Carlos Baleba and the Liverpool pair of Jérémy Jacquet and Víctor Muñoz could also receive debut patches.
